title: Find the full subject
prompt: The basketball court opens till ten at night on weekends.
hints: Ask who or what opens.
Do not choose only the head noun.
The full subject is the basketball court.
scaffold: Find the verb first, then ask who or what does that action.

title: Full subject in a noun phrase
prompt: My neighbour's three cats love that tree.
hints: Ask who loves that tree.
The owner phrase is part of the subject.
Choose the full subject, not only the head noun.
scaffold: A subject can be a noun phrase with describing words before the head noun.

title: Ignore opening phrase
prompt: With rising costs, Mr Tan saves money by not taking the taxi.
hints: With rising costs is an opening phrase.
Find who saves money.
Mr Tan is the subject.
scaffold: Opening phrases often give context but are not the subject.

title: Subject number
prompt: With rising costs, Mr Tan saves money by not taking the taxi. The subject is ____.
hints: The subject is Mr Tan.
Mr Tan refers to one person.
One person is singular.
scaffold: First find the subject, then decide if it names one or more than one.

title: Subject after time phrase
prompt: On Tuesdays, the generous hawker distributes free meals to needy residents.
hints: On Tuesdays is a time phrase.
Ask who distributes free meals.
The generous hawker is the subject.
scaffold: Ignore the time phrase and look for who performs the verb.

title: Singular subject
prompt: On Tuesdays, the generous hawker distributes free meals to needy residents. The subject is ____.
hints: The subject is the generous hawker.
Hawker names one person.
The subject is singular.
scaffold: Use the head noun to decide singular or plural.

title: Subject with possessive noun
prompt: On Mondays, Mr Ali's stall serves spaghetti and macaroni.
hints: Ask what serves spaghetti and macaroni.
Mr Ali owns the stall, but the stall serves.
The subject is Mr Ali's stall.
scaffold: A possessive noun can describe the subject but may not itself be the head noun.

title: Plural head noun
prompt: At the park, the wooden benches line the edge of the lake. The subject is ____.
hints: The subject is the wooden benches.
Benches names more than one bench.
The subject is plural.
scaffold: Ignore the place phrase and check the head noun.

title: Compound subject
prompt: Over several months, Mary's poor eyesight and carelessness have caused her to break many fragile items.
hints: Over several months is not the subject.
Ask what has caused her to break items.
Two ideas joined by and form the subject.
scaffold: Look for the verb phrase have caused, then ask what caused the action.

title: Plural subject regular verb
prompt: The ladies in pink ____ the dance well.
hints: The subject is the ladies.
Ladies is plural.
Plural subjects usually use the base verb perform.
scaffold: Find the subject number before choosing the verb.

title: Plural school groups
prompt: At the zoo, the school groups ____ a rare view of the shy panda.
hints: At the zoo is an opening phrase.
The subject is the school groups.
Groups is plural, so use catch.
scaffold: Ignore the opening phrase and match the verb to groups.

title: Singular dog
prompt: The big brown dog ____ to the park with its owners.
hints: The subject is the big brown dog.
Dog is singular.
A singular subject uses goes.
scaffold: For one animal or person, present tense often adds -s or -es.

title: Plural students
prompt: The students ____ their homework after school at the library.
hints: The subject is the students.
Students is plural.
Use do with plural subjects.
scaffold: Do and does also follow subject-verb agreement.

title: Spelling change: try
prompt: Although the boxes are heavy, the little boy ____ very hard to lift them.
hints: The subject is the little boy.
Boy is singular.
Try changes to tries for a singular subject.
scaffold: Check the true subject, not the nearby plural noun boxes.

title: Correct the verb error
prompt: On Tuesdays, the elderly librarian arrange the books at the children's section.
hints: The subject is the elderly librarian.
Librarian is singular.
The verb should be arranges.
scaffold: For correction items, identify the subject first, then repair the verb.

title: Correct plural verb
prompt: Several students browses the picture books quietly.
hints: The subject is several students.
Students is plural.
Use browse, not browses.
scaffold: Plural subject means no -s on the present-tense verb.

title: Past be verb
prompt: Choose the sentence that shows correct subject-verb agreement.
answer: She was not at the dentist two days ago.
options: She was not at the dentist two days ago.
She were not at the dentist two days ago.
hints: She is singular.
Two days ago shows past time.
Use was with she in the past.
scaffold: Match the be verb to both subject and time.

title: Question with you
prompt: Choose the sentence that shows correct subject-verb agreement.
hints: The subject is you.
Use are with you in the present.
The correct question begins Are you.
scaffold: In questions, the be verb may come before the subject, but it still has to agree.

title: I am
prompt: I ____ excited about the school trip tomorrow.
hints: The subject is I.
Use am with I.
Tomorrow does not change I am here.
scaffold: Memorise the special pair: I am.

title: Singular monitor
prompt: On Mondays, our class monitor ____ on duty at the library.
hints: On Mondays is not the subject.
The subject is our class monitor.
Monitor is singular, so use is.
scaffold: Ignore the opening phrase and match is or are to the subject.

title: Plural children
prompt: At the playground, the children ____ happy to run around.
hints: At the playground is an opening phrase.
Children is plural.
Use are with plural subjects.
scaffold: Some plural nouns do not end in -s, such as children.

title: Correct be verb error
prompt: You was patient with the new members of the team.
hints: The subject is you.
In the past, use were with you.
Change was to were.
scaffold: When correcting, replace only the incorrect be verb.

title: Choose helping verb
prompt: The baker ____ preparing fresh bread for the customers.
hints: The subject is the baker.
Baker is singular.
Use is before preparing.
scaffold: A verb phrase still begins with a helping verb that must agree with the subject.

title: Plural helping verb
prompt: The volunteers ____ helping at the community centre.
hints: The subject is the volunteers.
Volunteers is plural.
Use are before helping.
scaffold: Match the first helping verb to the subject.

title: Collective noun check
prompt: The team practises every Friday. The subject is ____.
hints: The subject is the team.
Team names one group.
Treat the subject as singular here.
scaffold: Some nouns name a group but are treated as singular.

title: Information before head noun
prompt: The bright colourful puzzles ____ on the table.
hints: Bright and colourful describe the noun.
The head noun is puzzles.
Puzzles is plural, so use are.
scaffold: Ignore describing words before the head noun.

title: Long premodified subject
prompt: These exciting electronic action games ____ popular with the children.
hints: These, exciting, electronic, and action describe the noun.
The head noun is games.
Games is plural.
scaffold: Find the head noun at the end of the subject phrase.

title: Information after head noun
prompt: The boy with the red shoes ____ quickly.
hints: With the red shoes gives extra information.
The head noun is boy.
Boy is singular, so use runs.
scaffold: Ignore the phrase after the head noun when choosing the verb.

title: Plural head noun with phrase after
prompt: The books on the highest shelf ____ dusty.
hints: On the highest shelf is extra information.
The head noun is books.
Books is plural.
scaffold: Do not let the nearby singular noun shelf control the verb.

title: Relative clause: volunteers
prompt: The volunteers who work there ____ very kind.
hints: Who work there is a relative clause.
The main subject is the volunteers.
Volunteers is plural, so use are.
scaffold: Cross out the relative clause, then match the verb to the main subject.

title: Relative clause: dog
prompt: The spotted dog whose tail wags whenever it sees Sarah ____ friendly.
hints: Whose tail wags is extra information.
The main subject is the spotted dog.
Dog is singular, so use is.
scaffold: Do not match the verb to tail; match it to dog.

title: Relative clause: cats
prompt: Three cats that live together in the corner ____ playful.
hints: That live together is a relative clause.
The subject is three cats.
Cats is plural, so use are.
scaffold: Relative clauses add information but do not change the head noun.

title: And makes plural
prompt: The local residents and mayor ____ now planning to set up a garden.
hints: The subject joins residents and mayor with and.
And usually makes the subject plural.
Use are.
scaffold: When two subjects are joined by and, use a plural verb in most cases.

title: Or with plural nearest subject
prompt: Some money or funds ____ to be raised in time.
hints: The subjects are joined by or.
The nearer subject to the verb is funds.
Funds is plural, so use have.
scaffold: With or, the verb often agrees with the nearer subject.

title: And with two plural food groups
prompt: Fruits and vegetables ____ going to be the main focus of the fair.
hints: Fruits and vegetables are joined by and.
The subject is plural.
Use are.
scaffold: Two joined subjects normally need a plural verb.

title: And with abstract nouns
prompt: Everyone hopes that dedication and hard work ____ to success.
hints: Dedication and hard work are joined by and.
The joined subject is plural.
Use lead.
scaffold: Even abstract nouns can form a compound subject.
